Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

ggseg.extra 1.9.9.9144

This section becomes the 2.0.0 release notes at submission. It is the first CRAN release of ggseg.extra, the atlas-building package of the ggsegverse, renamed and restructured from ‘ggsegExtra’ for the ggsegverse 2.0 architecture. Every pipeline now returns a single ggseg_atlas object holding 2D polygons and 3D meshes together, and geometry shaping has moved out of atlas creation into cheap post-creation verbs you can retune without rebuilding. Twelve create_*() entry points cover cortical, subcortical, cerebellar, whole-brain and white-matter tract atlases, built from FreeSurfer annotations and labels, GIFTI, CIFTI, neuromaps, NIfTI/MGZ parcellation volumes and tractography files.

Breaking changes

  • The package is ggseg.extra; the old ggsegExtra name is gone.

  • ggseg.formats moves from Imports to Depends, so library(ggseg.extra) attaches the whole atlas vocabulary. The re-exports are gone with it, so ggseg.extra::atlas_view_keep() and the like no longer resolve – call them unqualified, or as ggseg.formats::atlas_view_keep().

  • A label the lookup table does not list is not drawn. Declare a label to draw it.

  • A context value other than yes or no names a group, and every row carrying that name is traced as one silhouette called after it.

  • In create_subcortical_from_volume() the lookup table decides what is a region and what is context; nothing is recognised by id or name. A row whose context column is TRUE is context. Mark the cortex with lut$context <- grepl("Cortex", lut$label), and drop context you do not want with atlas_context_remove().

  • Geometry shaping is no longer part of atlas creation. dilate, smoothness, tolerance and smooth_refinements are rejected by every create_*(); use atlas_polish(), or atlas_simplify(), atlas_smooth() and atlas_dilate() on the finished atlas.

  • The ggseg.extra.tolerance and ggseg.extra.smoothness options and their GGSEG_EXTRA_* environment variables are removed.

  • atlas_smooth() and atlas_polish() default to method = "chaikin", which preserves sulci. Atlases smoothed with the default want rebuilding; pass method = "close" for the old behaviour.

  • atlas_smooth() and atlas_simplify() do one thing each; keep belongs to atlas_simplify().

  • atlas_view_remove_sparse() drops the views a build left nearly empty, counting what each view holds rather than naming views to remove. atlas_view_region_counts() reports the counts.

  • The colour-table functions are named after lookup tables: read_lut(), write_lut(), is_lut() and get_lut(). The *_ctab() spellings are removed.

  • sitrep() replaces setup_sitrep(), and ggseg_atlas_github_actions() replaces atlas_github_actions().

  • The volumetric creators take views, and subcortical_views() builds the table: each row is one view of the built atlas, its name becoming the view that ggseg.formats::atlas_views() reports. The slabs spelling used during the 2.0 dev cycle is deprecated and still works.

  • Related arguments are grouped into lists: tube_opts in create_tract_from_tractography(); labels, projection_opts, cortical_opts, subcortical_opts and cerebellar_opts in create_wholebrain_from_volume().

  • create_cerebellar_from_volume() takes input_volume first, and read_neuromaps_volume() takes breaks second and output_dir last.

  • mri_surf2surf_rereg() takes hemisphere rather than hemi.

  • registration means one thing across the package: "mni152", "header", or a path to a register.dat or LTA file. registration = NULL and regheader are gone; pass projection_opts = list(registration = ).

  • breaks replaces n_bins in create_cortical_from_neuromaps(), read_neuromaps_annotation() and read_neuromaps_volume(): a bin count, the edges, or a function returning them. Both hemispheres share one set of edges.

  • read_tractography() returns .trk streamlines in RAS world millimetres and reads big-endian files. create_tract_from_tractography() no longer accepts coord_space = "voxel" for tractography files.

  • create_wholebrain_from_volume() registers MNI152 volumes with FreeSurfer’s average/mni152.register.dat. Cortical atlases built from MNI152 volumes must be rebuilt.

  • Subcortical and tract contours are traced from the projection matrix rather than from a PNG of it (#139). Atlases built with earlier versions need rebuilding, and atlas_dilate(amount = ) and atlas_smooth(smoothness = ) now mean voxels rather than canvas pixels.

  • The subcortical pipeline has six steps and the tract pipeline four, and steps is bounds-checked.

  • skip_existing defaults to FALSE, and every reuse is reported naming the step.

  • Cerebellar region names come from label_to_region(), which strips vermis and midline alongside left and right. Names change on the next rebuild; label is unchanged.

  • The cerebellar flatmap gets a cerebellum backdrop, and perimeter regions are no longer inflated to the flatmap edge. Rebuilding changes geometry slightly.

  • Every cortical atlas keeps its unknown medial wall as grey context: no core row, no palette entry, no 3D vertices.

  • 2D geometry keeps its holes; coords2sf() assembles rings as exterior plus holes. Every atlas built through get_contours() differs from one built before.

  • The cortical creators have no method, snapshot_dim or steps arguments.

  • ggseg_atlas_repos(), install_ggseg_atlas() and install_ggseg_atlas_all() are removed; installing atlases is ‘ggsegverse’s job. convert_legacy_brain_atlas() lives in ’ggseg.formats’ and is re-exported here.

  • The dependency footprint is much lighter. chromote, magick, htmlwidgets, rgdal, purrr, reticulate and tidyr are gone; freesurfer (>= 1.9.0), freesurferformats, ciftiTools (>= 0.17.4), gifti, RNifti, Rvcg, terra, smoothr, princurve, rgl, neuromapr, ggseg and future are Suggests, checked at run time.

  • region is derived from the region’s identifier rather than copied from it. A lookup table that declares a region column is used as given. label is unchanged.

  • The core display column is display, following ggseg.formats.

  • hemi is "left", "right" or "midline" only. The vermis is "midline"; "vermis" and "middle" are still read as input.

New features

  • atlas_view_remove_empty() drops views that draw no region at all; ggseg.formats::atlas_views_empty() reports them without removing them.

  • Cerebellar atlases are a first-class type, with SUIT flatmap polygons for 2D and per-region meshes for 3D. create_cerebellar_from_gifti(), create_cerebellar_from_annotation() and create_cerebellar_from_volume() build them, and read_suit_parcellation() reads SUIT-format GIFTI labels.

  • Deep cerebellar nuclei with volume voxels but no SUIT surface vertices are tessellated as individual meshes and drawn as a separate coronal nuclei view. Surface parcels too small for any SUIT vertex are rescued onto the flatmap.

  • create_wholebrain_from_volume() builds cortical, subcortical and cerebellar sub-atlases from a single volumetric parcellation, classifying each label from the lookup table and reporting what it had to infer.

  • create_tract_from_tractography() builds a tract atlas from .trk/.tck files or coordinate matrices, and create_tract_from_volume() from a volumetric tract label map via principal-curve centerlines. Both produce 3D tubes and 2D slice projections.

  • create_wm_from_volume() builds a white-matter atlas from a label volume: the subcortical pipeline typed "wm".

  • create_cortical_from_cifti() and read_cifti_annotation() read CIFTI dense label files, and read_cifti_subcortical() extracts a CIFTI file’s subcortical voxels into a NIfTI volume plus colour table (#85). GIFTI .label.gii annotations are supported throughout.

  • create_cortical_from_neuromaps(), read_neuromaps_annotation() and read_neuromaps_volume() build atlases from neuromaps surface and volume annotations, binning continuous maps into regions.

  • The cortical pipeline projects inflated mesh triangles straight to 2D polygons. Atlas creation takes about five seconds rather than minutes, and the geometry carries no rasterisation staircase.

  • Boundary triangles spanning regions are split along edge midpoints, so borders are clean rather than sawtoothed, and boundary faces go to the smallest neighbouring region so tiny parcels survive.

  • A cortical parcellation covering only part of the mantle gets the rest as a silhouette to sit on (#285): one lh_cortex/rh_cortex region per hemisphere, drawn behind the parcellation with no colour or legend entry. A sparse cerebellar parcellation gets a single cerebellum backdrop.

  • atlas_polish() simplifies and smooths in one call against a stated vertex budget (#186).

  • atlas_smooth() gains method – "close", "chaikin", "ksmooth" and "spline", the last three keeping enclosed holes open – a smoothness strength on one 0–1 scale, and vertex_budget.

  • atlas_dilate() grows or shrinks region geometry on a finished atlas.

  • count_vertices() reports how many polygon vertices each region carries.

  • context_pattern() gives the label pattern matching an atlas’s context. atlas_polish(), atlas_simplify(), atlas_smooth() and atlas_dilate() accept a function as labels or exclude, so exclude = context_pattern works mid-pipe.

  • label_to_region() is exported: the rule the pipelines use to fill an atlas’s region column from its labels.

  • A lookup table can declare type, hemi and context columns, which the creators honour rather than guessing; write_lut() and read_lut() carry them through a round trip as a FreeSurfer-readable colour table. A declared hemisphere stops a midline-crossing parcel becoming two regions. aseg_subcortical_labels() returns the lumped structure ids a finer parcellation subdivides.

  • lut_classify_anatomy() fills a lookup table’s type column by resampling FreeSurfer’s aparc+aseg onto the volume’s grid and judging each label on the grey matter it touches, rather than by matching names.

  • lut_generate_colors() builds a palette for a names-only lookup table, assigning one colour per structure so its two hemispheres share it. by colours each group of a column from the whole circle.

  • lut_add() and lut_combine() append and merge colour tables, warning on index clashes.

  • subcortical_slabs() builds a slab table from the bounding box of a set of labels, and create_subcortical_from_volume(slabs = ) accepts that spec directly.

  • coregister_volume() aligns an atlas volume to a FreeSurfer subject’s T1 grid, project_volume_anatomical() resamples labels onto the target aparc+aseg grid, and prepare_subcortical_anatomical() chains both. id_offset avoids id collisions and protect_cortex keeps the ribbon intact for the brain outline.

  • prepare_subcortical_mni152() embeds an FSL-MNI152 parcellation into a subject’s aseg via mni152.register.dat. create_subcortical_from_volume() accepts its list(volume, lut, id_offset) directly as input_volume.

  • create_wholebrain_from_volume() gains cerebellar_opts = list(cerebellar_space = ), so an MNI cerebellar volume is transformed with the matching SUIT deformation field before being sampled onto the flatmap.

  • The tract creators gain coord_space, to declare whether streamline coordinates are "voxel" indices or RAS world "mm".

  • create_wholebrain_from_volume(context_opts = list(silhouette = "aseg")) substitutes FreeSurfer’s gyrified aseg ribbon for the parcellation’s own cortical labels. It is another subject’s anatomy, so it is asked for rather than inferred, and the pipeline reports which silhouette it drew.

  • setup_atlas_repo() scaffolds an atlas package from the ggseg-atlas-template repository, falling back to a bundled template when offline. use_atlas_github_actions() adds the shared workflows as caller stubs, and ggseg_atlas_github_actions() lists what is available.

  • sitrep() reports whether each of the 13 pipelines is ready to run.

  • clear_atlas_cache() removes build intermediates, refusing a directory holding files this package did not write.

  • Verbosity has three levels, resolved from an argument, the ggseg.extra.verbose option or GGSEG_EXTRA_VERBOSE, with get_verbose() and as_verbosity() as accessors. cleanup and output_dir resolve the same way.

  • Pipeline intermediates are cached per step, recording the cache format version that wrote them, so an older cache is recomputed rather than silently reused. Subcortical snapshots carry a signature of the voxels, slab and dimensions they were drawn from, and only what moved is redrawn.

  • Volumetric and tract builds parallelise through furrr: on eight cores create_subcortical_from_volume() goes from 337s to 171s with four workers.

  • The atlas_* verbs from ggseg.formats are re-exported, along with ggseg_atlas() and is_ggseg_atlas() (#186).

  • decimate reduces per-region 3D mesh vertex counts, and vertex_size_limits filters finished 2D polygons by vertex count.

  • The readers are exported: read_lut(), read_tractography(), read_annotation_data(), read_cifti_annotation(), read_cifti_subcortical(), read_gifti_annotation(), read_neuromaps_annotation(), read_neuromaps_volume() and read_suit_parcellation(). Volume reading reorients .mgz to RAS+ as it has for NIfTI.

Improvements

  • The flatmap projection is no longer cerebellum-specific: the surface path, backdrop label and small-area thresholds are supplied by the caller, so a second unfolded anatomy can reuse it. The thresholds have no defaults, being in the surface’s own units. Cerebellar atlas building is unchanged.

  • Every create_*() takes min_coverage: an atlas whose 2D geometry covers less than 80% of its core labels warns and names the labels with no shape.

  • The large-atlas warning has a per-atlas-type vertex budget, each just above its type’s 90th percentile across 109 installed atlases, and its advice names atlas_polish().

  • Data loss is reported whatever the verbosity: a structure that fails to tessellate, a degenerate centerline, a label dropped for too few voxels, a missing FreeSurfer installation and a dropped cerebellar nucleus are all named. verbose silences progress chatter only.

  • create_wholebrain_from_volume() says what it inferred and what it lost: labels classified by vertex count rather than declaration, labels assumed subcortical, parcels the projection did not deliver, and parcels landing on both surfaces.

  • A mistyped label in labels$cortical, labels$subcortical or labels$cerebellar is reported rather than dropped, and an unaccepted type or hemi value errors before any projection work.

  • lh and rh are read as a hemisphere only as a prefix, a suffix, or a token between separators, so Entorhinal is no longer right-hemisphere.

  • A region named in core but absent from the geometry is dropped from core, palette, meshes_df, vertices_df and vol_idx, with the dropped labels named; a build left with nothing to draw aborts.

  • atlas_smooth() no longer multiplies an atlas’s vertex count. It and atlas_simplify() close the hairline gaps they would otherwise open along shared boundaries while leaving genuine anatomical gaps open, controlled by close_gaps. atlas_simplify() preserves row order, which is draw order.

  • The grey outline behind a subcortical atlas sorts to the bottom layer in every view, including the per-hemisphere cortex_left/cortex_right names, so it no longer paints over its own structures.

  • The default subcortical slabs tile the bounding box of the atlas’s own labels – three coronal, three axial, one sagittal – rather than indices calibrated on a 256-cube, so no panel is empty whatever the voxel size. The sagittal slab is clipped to the left of the midline and named sagittal_left.

  • The context silhouette is taken from a single representative slice per view rather than projected through the slab, and is never dilated – all of which used to flatten the mantle into a blob.

  • Label ids colliding with the FreeSurfer indices the silhouette uses are moved onto free values before the volume and lookup table are written, so a real structure no longer absorbs the silhouette.

  • registration = "mni152" refuses a volume in right-handed (RAS) voxel order rather than silently mirroring left and right, and registered surface projections pass --srcsubject so labels come back as integers.

  • Volume handling is honest about what it can place: read_volume() says when it cannot orient an MGZ, coord_to_voxel()’s fallback reads the voxel size from the header, and create_tract_from_volume() declares coord_space = "mm".

  • FreeSurfer’s own output travels with a failure: stderr is captured whatever the verbosity, quoted in the error and chained as Caused by error:. A failing command carries the condition class ggseg_extra_fs_command_error.

  • A build with cleanup = TRUE cannot delete files it did not write: every create_*() stops when output_dir/atlas_name already holds files an earlier build did not make. atlas_name must be a single name.

  • Mistakes are reported before the expensive work: an unknown view or hemisphere, a missing input_aseg, an unusable breaks, a missing volume.

  • cleanup no longer deletes a cache the next run needs: a run stopping short of the last step keeps its working directory and says which steps can reuse it.

  • Arguments are validated before work starts – steps, smoothness, decimate, registration, tube_segments and the grouped lists – with an invalid grouped list reported against the argument the caller passed.

  • Every function orders its arguments the same way, and mistyped or misplaced arguments are caught by rlang::check_dots_empty().

  • Pipelines are faster where it counts: the label-stamping loops make one pass over the volume instead of one per label (about 44x on a 400-parcel atlas, byte-identical output), the per-voxel argmax streams the running winner, and read_tractography() reads .tck files without a quadratic slow-down.

  • Pipelines report their total run time, extracting contours no longer attaches terra to the search path, and a relative output_dir is made absolute on every platform.

Bug fixes

  • Building an atlas warns when its vertex indices do not fit the vertex space its type implies. The 2D geometry is unaffected, so it warns rather than failing.

  • labels and exclude are honoured exactly: geometry an operation was not asked to touch comes back byte-identical. atlas_smooth(), atlas_simplify(), atlas_polish() and atlas_dilate() previously rewrote excluded labels.

  • Slivers reopened by smoothing or simplifying go to a label the operation was asked to touch, so they are closed rather than reverted.

  • Subcortical 3D meshes are placed in the volume’s own world coordinates. Tessellation emits tkRAS, which is the identity only for a conformed volume; for a volume in its own space the axes are permuted and, where the handedness differs, left and right are swapped.

  • mri_vol2vol is given a transform FreeSurfer 8 accepts: the mni152.register.dat matrix is converted to an LTA against the volumes being registered. Affected prepare_subcortical_mni152() and coregister_volume().

  • A parcellation on a grid too coarse to carry a cortical ribbon is resampled onto the aseg’s grid rather than the aseg down to it, so the backdrop keeps its sulci instead of falling back to a solid mantle.

  • create_wholebrain_from_volume() declares the backdrop it writes, so the subcortical atlas keeps its grey brain silhouette.

  • An atlas whose lookup table carries no colours ships no palette, and says so, instead of one the pipeline invented. An atlas published with a palette still uses it.

  • A step’s cache records what it was built from – the package version, the cache format and the step’s own inputs – and recomputes when any of it moves.

  • read_lut() keeps a context group name instead of flattening it to TRUE, reads a label containing a space as a single token, and no longer truncates label names to 29 characters. write_lut() holds every column to a standard that keeps the round trip lossless.

  • The workflow templates use_atlas_github_actions() writes resolve dependencies against the ggsegverse r-universe.

  • display holds the source’s own name for a region again, rather than a copy of the derived region.

  • The cerebellar pipeline builds label from the source name rather than the derived region, so a published cerebellar atlas’s join and palette key is not rewritten.

  • The tract pipeline prunes snapshots its slabs cannot name, as the subcortical one did, so a projection left by an earlier slab configuration no longer aborts the build on a cache-format mismatch.

  • The cerebellar orphan rescue only considers vertices the flatmap triangulation uses, so a region is no longer rescued onto a vertex that belongs to no face and then dropped for having no geometry. A structure that reaches no drawable vertex says so.

  • default_tract_slabs() takes three axial and three coronal slabs, as default_subcortical_slabs() does, and drops the ones no label reaches. The three sagittal slabs stay for the commissural tracts.

  • create_subcortical_from_volume(), create_tract_from_tractography() and create_tract_from_volume() return the atlas they built rather than NULL.

  • read_tractography() reads a .tck file from where its header says the track data starts, aborts rather than fabricating coordinates for a truncated .trk, reports a header declaring more streamlines than the file holds, and reads to the end when the declared count is 0.

  • create_tract_from_tractography() turns streamlines to run the same way before computing a centerline, so a bundle stored in both directions is no longer shortened or collapsed. It also names an atlas after its tract rather than after the temporary directory.

  • A tract atlas’s sagittal_left and sagittal_right show the hemisphere they are named for, placed from where the brain sits in input_aseg.

  • Tract 2D projections line up with the anatomical reference and reuse the same centerline as the 3D tube; n_points reaches the tube in create_tract_from_volume().

  • tube_radius = "density" uses the middle of density_radius_range rather than silently producing the widest possible tube.

  • read_neuromaps_volume() keeps a parcellation a parcellation: a volume of whole-number labels, or one given a label_table, is sampled with nearest-neighbour interpolation instead of being blended and binned.

  • An atlas built from a .nii.gz without an atlas_name is named after the file, not <name>_nii.

  • prepare_subcortical_mni152() reports a FreeSurfer step that produced nothing, and the lookup-table readers accept a file write_lut() wrote.

  • sitrep() no longer reports create_cortical_from_annotation() as needing FreeSurfer, and suggests installing neuromapr from CRAN.

  • tessellate_remap_label() writes its isolated label back carrying the original affine, so a .mgz no longer loses every structure with a label id above 255 – the normal case for thalamic nuclei, hippocampal subfields and brainstem substructures.

  • A subcortical rebuild no longer reuses snapshots drawn from a different volume; each is checked against its signature, a changed slabs is honoured, and steps = 1:4 no longer deletes every snapshot in the cache.

  • Contours are no longer traced from files belonging to a different slab configuration, and a contour file matching none of the atlas’s views aborts naming it.

  • Subcortical and tract 2D views are no longer upside down, mirrored or drawn in the wrong plane, and contours record that their y-axis points up.

  • create_wholebrain_from_volume() no longer leaves white holes in the cortical atlas: the volume is filtered to the lookup table before projection, unlabelled cortex vertices take their neighbours’ most common label, and cortex is split at the correct 1-based midline voxel. It also handles lookup tables carrying labels with spaces.

  • The brain silhouette behind a subcortical atlas is no longer built from the atlas’s own parcels when their ids land between 1000 and 2999.

  • create_cerebellar_from_volume() builds from float-typed volumes, volume is forwarded by the GIFTI and annotation creators so their atlases carry 3D meshes, and decimate is honoured by all three.

  • create_cortical_from_neuromaps() honours label_table on the volume path, and tied values no longer abort with 'breaks' are not unique.

  • create_cortical_from_labels() and create_tract_from_tractography() keep region names when input_lut is a file path.

  • read_cifti_annotation() and create_cortical_from_cifti() work on real CIFTI files, warn when a file carries subcortical voxels the cortical pipeline ignores (#85), and warn on more than one label map.

  • atlas_dilate() with a negative amount large enough to erode a region away warns naming the regions lost and removes them, so the result still validates.

  • project_volume_anatomical() warns when protect_cortex removes a label entirely, naming the lost labels.

  • Annotation files whose colour table already defines unknown no longer produce a duplicate label, and parcellations naming their medial wall are treated as context while parcels such as medialorbitofrontal stay regions.

  • Contour extraction no longer crashes on empty or all-NA rasters, keeps the valid contours when only some are empty, and errors clearly when none yields a contour.

  • Suggested packages are checked before use in every path that needs them, and ensure_fs_compatible_nifti() falls through gracefully when a NIfTI header cannot be read.

  • prepare_subcortical_mni152() converts the aseg through freesurfer::mri_convert() (#118), paths containing spaces work, and region names containing () or / are handled throughout.

  • Boolean and verbosity options parse spelled-out strings consistently across the argument, option and environment-variable channels.

  • The bundled atlas template generates a package that passes R CMD check, and setup_atlas_repo() no longer copies the template’s own .github/ directory or rewrites files under .git.

Documentation

  • ?ggseg.extra states what these atlases are for: visualising results as general anatomical guidance, not precision geometry for analysis. It says which approximations are acceptable by design and which are bugs.

  • Six vignettes – getting started, pipeline configuration, post-processing, system setup, legacy conversion, contributing – and, on the website, an atlas creation workflows article plus nine step-by-step tutorials covering every pipeline.

  • The tutorials are built from reproducible .qmd.orig sources, plot the atlas at each stage of a build, and teach the current API. Five are knitted on every pull request.

  • vignette("post-processing") leads with atlas_polish() and treats polishing a context silhouette and a structure core as separate problems.

  • Examples for the geometry verbs run under R CMD check, and a test parses every documented example and asserts each argument it names is one the function accepts.

  • Help pages are scannable: @param says what to pass, with reasoning in @details; the twelve create_*() functions share @family atlas creation; every creator describes what its returned object holds.

  • The reference index groups geometry shaping, curation and file reading under their own headings, the re-exported atlas_* verbs have a visible ?atlas-verbs page, and the website separates Articles from Tutorials.

  • Reading annotation files needs the freesurferformats package, not a FreeSurfer installation, and SystemRequirements no longer claims FreeSurfer for the tract pipelines.
